name: Document layered architecture diagram
description: Layered architecture diagram for documentation: horizontal layering from top to bottom. The left side of each layer is the name and description, and the right side is the module label; click on the module to display the responsibility description and source code path below.
scenarios: Explain which layers the system consists of and what modules each layer has.
Match modules and source code paths in the architecture document
Explain the request from the entry layer all the way to the storage layer

boundaries: Suitable for hierarchical structures with 2–6 layers and 1–8 modules per layer; the default is top-down dependency between layers.
Please use doc-diagram for specific connections between modules.
reuse.owner: ShowAI document component library (doc-*), used for pages in showai.renaissancemind.ai/doc

usage.purpose: Use a hierarchical diagram to illustrate the architecture, and put the module's responsibilities and source code path into detail / path, and readers can click to view it.
structure: Middle part: layered from top to bottom, with thin downward connecting lines between layers.
Below: Description panel of the selected module (layer/module name, source code path, description).
When the width is less than 640px, the name of each layer is at the top and the module label is at the bottom.

inputs.meaning: Hierarchical, arranged from top to bottom (usually from entrance to storage). When empty, an empty status prompt is displayed.
Layer name, 2–6 Chinese characters are recommended.
A description of the layer, displayed below the name.

omission.description: Only the layer name is displayed.

inputs.meaning: Layer tones: brand | teal | warm | violet | rose | slate. Used for serial numbers, module dots and selected status.

omission.description: Use brand, teal, violet, warm, rose, slate in order of layers.

inputs.meaning: Modules of this layer are displayed as clickable labels. It can be an empty array (displaying "No module yet"). No more than 8 per layer is recommended.
Module name, it is recommended not to exceed 10 characters.
The source code path or directory is displayed in the description panel in fixed-width font.

omission.description: The description panel does not display the path.

inputs.meaning: Module responsibilities description. Supports **bold**,`代码`, [Link](https://…) and [Link](doc:slug#anchor); line break segmentation.
A description above the figure supports inline markup.
Initial selected module: module name, or "layer name/module name" (used when the module name is repeated in multiple layers).

omission.description: If it is not selected initially, the description panel will display a prompt; if it cannot be found, the same process will be performed.

recipes.title: Draw an architecture layered diagram
steps: List the layers from top to bottom from user portal to storage.
At each layer, only the modules that readers need to know are listed, write a sentence of responsibility and check the source code path.
Use initial to select the modules focused on in this section.

interactions.action: Click the module label or select with Tab / Enter
interactions.effect: Select the module and display the description and path below; click Cancel again.
Move between modules on the same layer; use the up and down arrow keys to cross layers.

constraints: Reading operations do not modify page data.

data: When modifying the module, check that path exists in the repository.
implementation: Create a new version when horizontal columns or specific connections between layers are needed.

entryPoints.purpose: Layered rendering, selection state, keyboard navigation and readData.
Tokens, light and dark themes, layered and narrow screen layouts.

architecture: Pure HTML / CSS layout: each layer is a two-column grid, which becomes a single column for narrow screens; the connecting lines between layers are decorative SVG.
extensionPoints: When no tone is specified, press ORDER to select colors in sequence.
invariants: Only react is imported; inline markup is rendered as React elements.
Reading interactions only change local state.
verification: The example "ShowAI Architecture" should show 4 layers, with MCP initially selected and src/agent/mcp.ts displayed.
Check module wrapping and alignment in light, dark and 390px width.

modules.name: block
modules.detail: Paragraphs, headings, components in the document flow, each block has a stable id.

modules.name: container
modules.detail: Page and Board can be nested within each other.

modules.name: Built-in components
modules.detail: Charts, maps, tables, etc. are provided with the application.

modules.name: Custom component
modules.detail: React package, the exact version of which the page refers to.

examples.name: ShowAI architecture: entry layer, workbench, core, component runtime

data.caption: From entry to file: All entries call the same set of TypeScript Core, and the content is ultimately an ordinary file in the content library.

modules.name: Desktop version
modules.detail: Electron App comes with its own runtime, and the window configuration is saved in the system application data directory.

modules.name: local browser
modules.detail: The workbench started by `showai serve `only listens to the loopback address and uses SSE to push file changes.

modules.name: CLI
modules.detail: The command line is executed on demand. The Agent can read and write pages without relying on desktop windows or resident services.

modules.name: MCP
modules.detail: The optional stdio MCP adapter provides **page_read**, **page_save**, **page_present** and other tools for Agents such as Codex and Claude Code.

modules.name: Shared workbench operation
modules.detail: The desktop version and the local service call the same implementation to ensure that the two entrances behave consistently.

modules.name: Page/Board Editor
modules.detail: The React editor uses the same page structure as the standalone reader.

modules.name: reader
modules.detail: The exported page uses the reading view, which can be interacted with without a workbench.

modules.name: storage
modules.detail: Read and write `projects/<id>/pages/<page-id>.json `, leaving a snapshot for each save.

modules.name: Table of contents
modules.detail: Analyze built-in, global and project-level components and templates, as well as their versions.

modules.name: diff and merge
modules.detail: The base hash is compared when saving. If the content has been modified by others, a difference and merge preview will be given instead of overwriting it directly.

modules.name: sandbox iframe
modules.detail: Custom components are rendered in the `allow-scripts `sandbox, strictly CSP, and cannot access the network.

modules.name: component package
modules.detail: Compiled components are stored in accurate versions, and only the components used on the page are collected during export.
